ALL-DAY FIRE ON DOCKED LINER.

The Canadian Pacific liner Montlaurier ablaze in dry dock at Birkenhead where she was undergoing repairs. The fire raged all day yesterday (Apl 15th), and the whole of the forepart of the ship was burnt out before the firemen completely quelled the outbreak in the early evening.
ATLANTIO LINER ALT BY TOBACCO....

The Canadian Liber Montrode, arriving at Liverpool with buns badly damaged by collision with an iceberg. Two of the crew were killed. One of the men was making his last trip before getting married....15 4 26

The lighthouses on the great lakes present a striking spectacle every winter, being covered in a thick mantle of ice. Our photograph depicts the Racine Reef Lighthouse, on Lake Michigan, taken in mid winter. This is one of the most exposed beacons on the great lakes. The building is an octagonal tower, with a pyramidal roof. When navigation ceases for the winter those towers are closed, the keepers are turning to them the moment the spring thawed not in. Even then they have often to out a passage through the thick ice to their lighthouse doors and for many days afterwards spend a weary and anxious time in clearing the ice away from the structures and repairing any damage inflicted upon the building by the winter storms.

What is declared to be the only unattended lighthouse built on a wave-washed rock, possessing a powerful fog signal which can be heard twenty-five miles and more away and a flashing light, is the recently completed Platte Fougere Lighthouse, marking the entrance to the Russell Charnel, leading to the Guernsey capital of St. Peter's Port, a spot which figures in Victor Hugo's great romance, 'The Toilers of the Sea'.

The tower is a ferroconcrete structure 80 feet in height. On its summit is placed an acetylene gas plant and light as well as a fog siren and several cylinders of compressed air used in working the fog signal. At sunset the light is automatically switched on from the shore station, 1$\frac{1}{2}$ miles distant, by means of an electric submarine cable, and at sunrise automatically extinguished. In the same way should the weather turn foggy the siren is set going to be suspended at the will of the operator.

The lighthouse is in charge of Mr. B.O.Catford, a clever electrician, who has devised several delicate instruments for ensuring the efficacy of this novel lighthouse without keepers. At every blast of the siren a bell is rung in the engine-room ashore. Should, for any reason, the light fail, a bell would announce that fact to those on land.
